attributes.decisive_finding: RESULT: EXACT + TU FLIPPED. GetAnimAngXYZVal real 172 -> 156 in source, then real 0 via an audited WebFrank copy_register_fields rule; game/anim/anim_play.c is now Matching (Game Code linked 43 -> 44 files, 9.96% -> 10.55%). THE AXIS AS NAMED WAS THE RIGHT TARGET BUT THE WRONG MECHANISM, AND v3's DO-NOT-RETRY WAS FACTUALLY WRONG. Correct decomposition, read from every N(r1) row on both sides: the high region [784,816) holds keynum-spill(4), bits-spill(4), the hoisted 0x43300000 int-to-double magic word(4), and TWO 8-byte doubles at 800 and 808. TARGET: keynum@784, DEAD@788, bits@792, magic@796, d2@800, d1@808. OURS was keynum@784, bits@788, magic@792, DEAD@796, d2@800, d1@808. Our dead word was NOT a misplaced reservation and NOT a pair-alignment defect: it was simply the 8-alignment PAD in front of the first 8-byte double, forced because our compiler-temp block started at the non-8-aligned 788. The target's block starts at the 8-aligned 792 and therefore needs no internal pad; its dead word at 788 is named-local storage sitting ABOVE keynum. So the requirement was exactly 4 more bytes of named storage above the first spilled local, which lifts the temp block base 788 -> 792 and makes the internal pad disappear. GA1 (ruler, u8 unusedTop[8] as the FIRST declaration) measured this directly and REFUTED v3: it was not inert at all - frame 920 -> 928, temp base 788 -> 796, bits 788 -> 796, magic 792 -> 800, d2 -> 808, d1 -> 816, stmw 816 -> 824, i.e. a clean 8-byte lift of the whole temp block with keynum held at its own slot. GA2 (the same declaration at u8[4]) gave SLOT MAP IDENTICAL, frame 920/920, 222/222 slots, real 172 -> 160. v3 recorded this exact form as producing a byte-identical slot map; it does not, and the 8-byte ruler proves the mechanism it was supposed to lack. Treat v3's 'function-scope declaration-position axis is closed from both ends' as withdrawn.

attributes.measurement_resolution: One 4-byte stack slot, arbitrated on slotdiff (frame, save set, slot sets, per-slot use counts) and on the aligned fnasm --diff view. The 8-byte ruler was run BEFORE the 4-byte form precisely because v3 had recorded the 4-byte form as inert - the ruler is what exposed that as false, and it is the cheapest possible way to re-test a suspect do-not-retry without re-running the vetoed probe first.
